summary: Round 3, narrow. All four round-2 fixes re-measured in a throwaway export of the staged index (gradle :format:test, 279 tests, no 'error:' in any build log) and all four die on their own assertion: decode's negative-expiry guard -> if(false) kills aNEGATIVEExpiryOnTheWireIsAnIOExceptionToo with 'Expecting actual throwable to be an instance of java.io.IOException but was java.lang.IllegalArgumentException'; Grant's 'millis < 0' -> if(false) kills aPreEPOCHExpiryIsRefused with 'Expecting code to raise a throwable'; 'grant' dropped from Objects.hash(...) kills aDifferingGRANTOrRANGEMakesTwoEventsUNEQUAL on 'a different grant is a different hash, with the range held equal'; equals dropping byteStart alone and byteLen alone each kill the same case on 'a different start alone' / 'and a different length alone'. The round-1 mutation 'Objects.equals(grant, that.grant) -> true' is also now killed. The hostile splice in aNEGATIVEExpiryOnTheWireIsAnIOExceptionToo is honest: the ten-byte all-ones varint reads back as -1 through Cursor.uvarint (shift reaches exactly 63, so the 'varint longer than 64 bits' refusal does not fire first), the body reaches the expiry guard rather than failing earlier -- proven by the if(false) run getting as far as new Grant(...) -- the arithmetic fills hostile exactly (flagAt-6 + 10 + 1 == good.length+4), and the assertion on good[flagAt] == 0 would fail rather than pass vacuously if the presence byte and the expiry swapped places. One new surviving mutation found outside the round-2 delta but inside the named scope: SubscriptionEvent.toString prints the grant, and its javadoc claims the URL never reaches that line, with nothing pinning it.

findings.title: SubscriptionEvent.toString's redaction claim has no case; printing grant.url() instead of grant leaves all 279 tests green
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a throwaway export of the staged index, no 'error:' in the build log: mutate line 369 from `+ ", grant=" + grant` to `+ ", grant=" + (grant == null ? null : grant.url())` and :format:test runs 279 tests with 0 failures. The three lines of javadoc directly above it assert the opposite -- 'THE GRANT PRINTS THROUGH ITS OWN REDACTION, so the URL never reaches this line' -- and that claim is in this diff. Grant.toString's redaction is pinned (GrantTest:28), but the composition point is not: SubscriptionEvent.toString is hand-written concatenation, is the line an operator prints while debugging a delivery (its own javadoc says so), and is interpolated into AssertJ descriptions and log lines. The precedent is in the same class: toStringCarriesNODocumentPayload (format/src/test/java/binjava/format/SubscriptionEventTest.java:418) exists precisely to pin security.md rule 4 for the inline payload, and it builds a FetchMode.INLINE event with no grant -- so the commit that added the grant field did not extend the one test that owns rule 4 for this type, and that file is not in the staged set at all. The concrete failure: a future edit (or a revert to the record's generated toString, which prints components verbatim) puts a full presigned URL with its signature into every log line that prints an event, and nothing in the tree goes red. The fix is additive and does not split the commit: one case constructing a grant-carrying event and asserting event.toString() doesNotContain the signature and contains 'redacted'.

findings.title: The new expiry guard's boundary is unpinned: `< 0` -> `<= 0` survives, reopening the encode/decode asymmetry at expiry zero
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, no compile error: mutate `if (expiresAtMillis < 0)` to `if (expiresAtMillis <= 0)` and all 279 tests pass. Grant's own bound accepts millis == 0 (`if (millis < 0)`), so `new Grant(url, Instant.EPOCH)` constructs, the event encodes, and decode then refuses it with IOException 'a grant expiry of 0 is not an instant' -- an event this class produces and cannot read back, which is exactly the defect class the commit closed twice already (the absent session epoch, and the negative byteStart whose case says 'it constructed and encoded and then decode refused it, so the constructor's own claim to keep the round trip total was false'). The value is degenerate (a grant that expired at 1970), which is why this is minor rather than major. review.md rule 11: recording it in the commit body or as a backlog row is the right answer, not a fourth round spent on it.

notes: Non-finding, stated so it is not chased: dropping byteStart or byteLen individually from Objects.hash(...) survives the suite -- the only hashCode pair held equal in the range differs in BOTH components. That is not a contract violation (hashCode is only required to agree with equals in the equal direction), so it is not a finding and should not be pinned.

Non-finding: aNEGATIVEExpiryOnTheWireIsAnIOExceptionToo asserts isInstanceOf(IOException.class) with no hasMessageContaining, unlike its three sibling crafted-byte cases (the range-present flag, the blank url, the v4 version). I could not name a production mutation that survives because of it -- with the guard disabled the escape is an IllegalArgumentException, so the type assertion alone is decisive today -- so this is durability, not a hole.
